record.what_it_does: Telegram is a cloud-based messaging platform that exposes a free HTTP-based Bot API for building bots/integrations and a lower-level MTProto Client API for building full client applications.
record.auth_notes: The Bot API is authenticated with a static bot token issued by @BotFather, embedded in the request URL path (e.g. https://api.telegram.org/bot<token>/METHOD) rather than a standard Authorization header — functionally a bearer token, not OAuth2, and it is not scoped per-end-user. There is no OAuth2 flow for third parties to act on behalf of arbitrary end users via the Bot API. Separately, the MTProto 'Client API' (for building user-facing apps) requires an api_id/api_hash pair from my.telegram.org plus full user login (phone number + code/2FA) over a custom binary protocol — classified here as 'Other' since it's neither OAuth2 nor a simple API key and requires per-user interactive login, making it unsuitable for a standard multi-tenant agent toolkit.
record.access_notes: Anyone can message @BotFather and get a working bot token immediately at no cost; the whole Bot Platform is documented as free for developers. The Client API (api_id/api_hash) is also free and self-serve via my.telegram.org, but usage is monitored for abuse and accounts can be banned/rate-limited if flagged, and it requires a real phone-verified account rather than a simple credential — so it's less turnkey than the Bot API.

record.open_questions: Could not confirm whether Telegram publishes a machine-readable OpenAPI/Swagger spec for the Bot API on a vendor page within the tool budget (only third-party generated specs are known); marked openapi_spec false pending further check. Bots also cannot initiate conversations with arbitrary users (a user must message/add the bot first), which may constrain some outbound-messaging agent use cases.
